smt-2018-calculus-tiebreaker-02.title: Termwise limits
smt-2018-calculus-tiebreaker-02.body:
Each term is a derivative: $\lim_{n\to1}\frac{n^k-1}{\ln n}=\lim\frac{kn^{k-1}}{1/n}=k$ (L'Hopital). The sum is finite, so the limit is $1+2+\cdots+25=\frac{25\cdot26}{2}=325$.

**Answer: 325**

smt-2018-calculus-tiebreaker-03.title: Expand
smt-2018-calculus-tiebreaker-03.body:
$\sin^{10}x=\frac1{2^{10}}\binom{10}{5}+(\text{terms in }\cos(2jx),\ j\ge1)$, and the cosine terms integrate to $0$ over $[0,\pi]$. So the integral is $\pi\binom{10}{5}/1024=\frac{252\pi}{1024}=\frac{63\pi}{256}$.

**Answer: $\frac{63\pi}{256}$**
